chapter: Violin, clarinet and the family name
title: Refusing the piano, playing violin, learning to box
summary: He refused the piano as a woman's instrument, played violin instead, and his father gave him boxing gloves to cope with teasing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: miss it. It wasn't forced on me at all. My father never forced anything on me. My mother never forced anything on me. They had an idea that they would have liked for me to have complete knowledge of the piano, which I positively refused to play, because I had the complex all built in my mind that a piano was only supposed to be played by a woman because my mother was a woman and she played the piano and I would be less than a man if I played the piano. I positively refused to play the piano.

But yet, I played the violin, which in the eyes of many, was considered as a sissy instrument. But my father was intelligent enough from the time that I got into junior high school playing the violin to also give me a set of boxing gloves, so that -- and sent me down to the gym to learn how to take care of myself, because he knew somebody was going to be picking at me because I was playing the violin.
So, I learned how to be a pretty good boxer by being a violin player.
